(2) _contained was check-then-use (resolved once to check, read_text re-resolved) -- a symlink swap between the two could be checked inside and read outside; now _resolved_within returns the resolved path and the read is taken from it (not atomic against a genuine race, but that needs write access inside the root, which already lets an attacker plant a control -- documented honestly, not overclaimed). (3) note() now counts Blocked explicitly instead of borne-failed, so a future Not Applicable can't be silently folded into Blocked. READINESS SEAM landed 2026-08-16 (docs/design/the-forge-readiness.md): stores/readiness_corpus.py measures the measuring panel's coverage against an EXTERNAL control corpus instead of the five classes the panel wrote for itself -- the sigmap trap one level up (a harness grading itself against a ruler it cut). The corpus is rudi193-cmd/production-readiness-checklist, a fork of MarinJursic/production-readiness-checklist (MIT, v2.1.0, released 2026-08-15): 10,042 technology-neutral controls with stable IDs (grounded: parsed 1,421 PRC-* + 8,621 USEQ-*, matching its own scripts/validate.py constants). INJECTED, NEVER VENDORED -- the Almanac seam one axis over (stores/almanac/README.md: 'ship the mold and the reader; the wood stays with whoever grew it'), applied to a public STANDARD rather than a public list: corpus root comes from an explicit path or FORGE_READINESS_CORPUS, no default, absence raises CorpusUnavailable as a declared gap. The two control regexes are lifted from the corpus's OWN validator (upstream owns its format; a format change is CorpusUnavailable, not a looser pattern). UNTRUSTED INPUT read as data: nothing imported or executed, every path checked to resolve inside the corpus root (a symlink planted in docs/checklists/ cannot smuggle a control in -- the crown-jewel containment check applied to an injected corpus), every control string NFKC-normalized with control chars dropped and capped at 300 chars so it cannot forge a line in a queue item. ONE-DIRECTIONAL: assess() can Fail a control, never Pass one -- a finding fails with artifact+metric+the control's own file:line cited; a clean instrument leaves it Blocked (absence of a finding is not evidence, the corpus's rule 6 and the Forge's thesis in one sentence); Status.PASS exists only because a HUMAN records one with evidence/owner/release/date, and _refuse_to_mint_pass() RAISES rather than returning, because a convention is what a later edit forgets. Bearings are hand-authored (4 instruments, 6 controls, each verified present in the real corpus by a live test) -- keyword-matching against 10,042 control texts would manufacture dozens of unearned mappings, exactly the inference rule 6 forbids. THE FIRST REAL RUN CORRECTED THE DESIGN: the census flagged the-binder/web/binder.png at 95% of the build and the seam called PRC-07-015 ('Large binaries, generated files, and vendored code are controlled') Fail -- but a 95% PNG is evidence a large binary EXISTS, not that large binaries are UNCONTROLLED, and rule 5's bar for Fail is direct evidence the control is NOT MET. So Bearing gained on_finding: census declares BLOCKED (names the artifact, says it raises the control without answering it) while hygiene finding a committed error_log genuinely fails it. Seven playground builds had been called Fail by the size census alone; all seven are now Blocked-with-the-artifact-named. A bearing may not claim a finding supports a Pass -- the constructor raises. calibration is deliberately absent from the table (longitudinal, a claim ACROSS builds, so it cannot bear on a control scoped to one release). NO PERCENTAGE is reported (the corpus's rule 13: one blocker outweighs hundreds of passing controls) -- raw counts and the reason the ratio is missing; two instruments disagreeing on one control resolve to a single status with Fail winning, the per-instrument verdicts kept as the evidence trail.
